Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (6) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Lost start records trigger another lead 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>start_after_alarm() uses a trusted LEAD-STARTED comment as its only durable evidence that the
>watchdog has fired the lead task. If the trigger succeeds but post_quietly() cannot publish that
>comment, start_lead() returns success and the next watchdog run can fire the task again for the
>same stall.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[3047]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/14/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3047-R3047) > >```diff >+ code, why = start_lead(a, a.room, "watchdog", takeover=takeover) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Lost LEAD-STARTED after a successful fire is an edge case; no historical precedent found.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new watchdog path suppresses another fire only when its comment scan finds LEAD-STARTED. The
>existing trigger path fires before attempting that post and returns success even when the post fails
>after retries.
>
> > [room.py\[3026-3047\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3026-L3047) > [room.py\[3752-3770\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3752-L3770) > [room.py\[3806-3817\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3806-L3817) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A successful task fire followed by a failed `LEAD-STARTED` post leaves no durable evidence of the watchdog's start, so its next run can fire again. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3031-3047] >- room.py[3807-3824] >## Recommended Fix >Give each stall a durable, once-only start claim before firing, and do not retry a fired or uncertain trigger solely because publishing its result failed. Preserve recovery for definite pre-fire failures. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. No automatic restart when a handover's successor dies 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>start_after_alarm treats any trusted LEAD-STARTED newer than since as the stall's one start
>(rule 2). On the ordinary path since is the last progress time, and cmd_handoff writes the step
>before the outgoing lead runs start-lead, so the successor's LEAD-STARTED is always newer than
>that progress. The result is that a successor whose start didn't take, or that joined and died
>before its first step change or push, gets alarms and reminders but never the watchdog start. The
>spec's per-path list ("released after a handover whose successor never came: one takeover or plain
>start") and the CHANGELOG and ARCHITECT text all promise that start.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3033-3037]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/14/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3033-R3037) > >```diff >+ started = [m for m in msgs if message_kind(m["text"]) == "LEAD-STARTED" and newer(m)] >+ if started: >+ print(f"note: LEAD-STARTED #{started[-1]['id']} at {started[-1]['at']} is this stall's start; the watchdog " >+ "starts no other") >+ return >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Real logic bug that contradicts the PR's stated intent (one start per stall after handover); the
>spec and CHANGELOG promise it.
>
> > [PR-#5](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>cmd_handoff writes step (the commit that sets progress), posts HANDOFF and releases the lease.
>Only after that does the lead run start-lead, which posts LEAD-STARTED with role lead.
>cmd_watchdog passes progress (the newest step/pr change or push) as since. So newer(m) is
>true for the handover's LEAD-STARTED, and start_after_alarm prints 'is this stall's start' and
>returns. The spec says this path should get one start. No test in tests/test_m6d.py covers a
>handover (no HANDOFF in the file).
>
> > [room.py\[3303-3326\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3303-L3326) > [room.py\[3029-3037\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3029-L3037) > [room.py\[3196-3214\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3196-L3214) > [docs/design/m6d-watchdog.md\[33-33\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/docs/design/m6d-watchdog.md/#L33-L33) > [room.py\[3769-3770\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3769-L3770) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >On the ordinary-stall path, `start_after_alarm` counts the handover's own `LEAD-STARTED` (posted by role `lead` right after `handoff` writes the step) as the stall's one start. As a result, the watchdog never starts a lead when a handover's successor fails to join or dies before making progress. The spec says this path gets one start. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3033-3037] >- docs/design/m6d-watchdog.md[13-13] >- tests/test_m6d.py[1-438] > >## Recommended Fix >Pick one of these and apply it everywhere: >- **Change the code to match the spec:** in rule 2, count only `LEAD-STARTED`s that aren't the handover's. For example, count only role `watchdog`/`architect` starts, or only starts newer than the first alarm of the stall. Then a lead-role `LEAD-STARTED` posted before the alarm doesn't use up the one start. >- **Change the docs to match the code:** remove the claim from the spec's per-path list, the CHANGELOG and ARCHITECT.md. > >Either way, add a test: HANDOFF, then a lead `LEAD-STARTED`, then no LEAD ONLINE, then the stall alarm. Assert the intended outcome. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/30007175-bf9b-4263-ab3a-04b17ea93b75?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/30007175-bf9b-4263-ab3a-04b17ea93b75)
3. Overlapping runs can start two leads 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>start_after_alarm() checks for an existing start and then calls start_lead() without atomically
>claiming the stall. If two watchdog runs overlap, both can pass that check and start_refusal()'s
>separate comment check before either posts LEAD-STARTED, allowing both to fire the task.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3046-3047]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/14/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3046-R3047) > >```diff >+ try: >+ code, why = start_lead(a, a.room, "watchdog", takeover=takeover) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Plausible race in overlapping watchdog runs, but speculative; no close precedent found either way.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Both the new watchdog check and the downstream refusal check read comments without reserving the
>stall; the task fire follows those reads.
>
> > [room.py\[3026-3047\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3026-L3047) > [room.py\[3724-3739\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3724-L3739) > [room.py\[3800-3811\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3800-L3811) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Concurrent watchdog runs can both observe an unstarted stall and fire its lead task. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3026-3047] >- room.py[3710-3739] >## Recommended Fix >Use an atomic, durable per-stall claim or equivalent serialization before the task fire. Ensure a losing run cannot proceed based on an earlier snapshot of room comments. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/ed3c6bb3-cf33-4209-8baa-47b890db11ed?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/ed3c6bb3-cf33-4209-8baa-47b890db11ed)
4. A renewed state outage misses its alarm 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>unreadable_state_alarm() now passes a predicate that keeps every earlier state-unreadable alarm
>since progress, even across an intervening ordinary alarm. If state recovers, an ordinary stall
>alarm is posted, and state becomes unreadable again without newer progress, stall_alarm() treats
>the previous outage's alarm and retry count as belonging to the new outage.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3108-3110]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/14/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3108-R3110) > >```diff >+ stall_alarm(a, progress, (f"state unreadable ({reason})", f"LEAD-SILENT: state unreadable ({reason})"), >+ (f"still state unreadable ({reason})", f"LEAD-SILENT: still state unreadable ({reason})"), >+ only=lambda m: re.search(r"LEAD-SILENT: (?:still )?state unreadable", m["text"]) is not None) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Cross-outage alarm counting edge case; related accepted watchdog-progress feedback exists, but no
>direct precedent.
>
> > [PR-#5](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/5) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>alarms_since() returns all matching-time watchdog alarms, and the new predicate removes
>intervening ordinary alarms before stall_alarm() decides whether to send a first alarm or retry.
>The ordinary-stall path can post such an intervening alarm.
>
> > [room.py\[2939-2944\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L2939-L2944) > [room.py\[2956-2983\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L2956-L2983) > [room.py\[3106-3110\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3106-L3110) > [room.py\[3205-3213\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3205-L3213) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Filtering all historical unreadable alarms carries their timing and failed-buzz retries into a later outage after an ordinary alarm. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[2956-2978] >- room.py[3106-3110] >## Recommended Fix >For the unreadable-state path, account only for the latest contiguous run of unreadable alarms since progress, resetting that run when another alarm type intervenes. Test outage, recovery, ordinary alarm, and renewed outage. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/5361ed9a-7333-46e3-b156-06bd6f3b0308?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/5361ed9a-7333-46e3-b156-06bd6f3b0308)

5. Other alarms delay owner reminders 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>cmd_watchdog() passes the waiting request's timestamp to stall_alarm() without restricting it to
>alarms about that request. If state was unreadable after the request and its alarm was posted before
>state recovered, the unreadable alarm counts as the waiting reminder and postpones the first
>reminder until its own 12-hour interval expires.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[3170]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/14/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3170-R3170) > >```diff >+ stall_alarm(a, t, waiting, waiting) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Unfiltered stall_alarm counting unrelated alarms is plausible; no direct precedent found.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new waiting path uses the request time with the default, unfiltered stall_alarm(). That
>function counts every watchdog LEAD-SILENT newer than the time, including a state-unreadable alarm
>that its separate path can post.
>
> > [room.py\[2939-2944\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L2939-L2944) > [room.py\[2956-2983\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L2956-L2983) > [room.py\[3106-3110\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3106-L3110) > [room.py\[3159-3170\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3159-L3170) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >An alarm for another condition can suppress the first reminder for an unanswered owner request. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[2956-2964] >- room.py[3166-3170] >## Recommended Fix >Select only waiting-for-Matthew alarms for the particular request when calculating its retries and reminder interval. Add a test with an intervening state-unreadable alarm. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/26c33dd0-7f48-4c2d-97d2-89c24be2ddd0?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/26c33dd0-7f48-4c2d-97d2-89c24be2ddd0)
6. Unrecorded rooms receive owner reminders 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>waiting_request() rejects a different current room but permits current_room() to return None.
>If the state says waiting for owner without a valid room in either the playbook or machine block,
>an old request in the watchdog's room can produce a reminder despite no record that this is the
>current room.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R3068-3069]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/14/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R3068-R3069) > >```diff >+ room = current_room(playbook, values) >+ if lease_of(values)[0] != "none" or (room and room[0] != a.room): >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Null-room edge case in waiting_request; plausible but no matching precedent found.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>current_room() explicitly returns None if neither source records a valid room, while the new
>guard rejects only a truthy, mismatching result. quiet_reason() can still select the waiting path
>and the new code posts a reminder from the old request.
>
> > [room.py\[2398-2407\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L2398-L2407) > [room.py\[2777-2791\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L2777-L2791) > [room.py\[3064-3081\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3064-L3081) > [room.py\[3159-3170\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/bc901b7bb45e50a86dc95aa3af100446c8faa6b6/room.py/#L3159-L3170) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The new reminder path accepts an absent current-room record as though it matched the watchdog's room. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[3064-3071] >## Recommended Fix >Require `current_room()` to return a room equal to `a.room` before looking for an unanswered request; otherwise remain quiet and report that the current room cannot be established. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
